item.title: Norway mourns King Harald as new era begins under Haakon VIII
item.description:
The new King and Queen of Norway, Mette-Marit and Haakon, are seen here at the Norwegian Constitution Day in Oslo on May 17, 2026. —Per Ole Hagen—Getty Images King Harald V of Norway, a reformer and Europe ’s oldest monarch, died Friday at the age of 89. His son, the newly-proclaimed King Haakon VIII, has inherited the Norwegian throne. Harald passed away peacefully in his sleep at Oslo University Hospital Rikshospitalet at 6:35 a.m., local time, the Royal Palace of Norway said . “A whole nation is in mourning and the people of Norway are left with a deep sense of gratitude for a long life in the service of Norway,” said Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre. “For more than three decades as monarch, Harald V demonstrated an unwavering faith in the Norwegian people. item.title: Lights out, Instagram off? The changes to Meta for teens could be a big deal
item.description:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg chose to settle a landmark lawsuit against his company. Jon Putman/Anadolu via Getty Images Meta has agreed to pay up to US$17 billion over 10 years to settle claims brought by a bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general. The states argued that the company deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to hook children into using its apps, misled the public about the harm and improperly collected data from children under 13. The settlement , announced by Meta on Aug. 26, 2026, ended a federal trial that had barely begun in Oakland, California. The potential financial exposure in the case was enormous, and Meta’s stock price took a hit. The states argued that penalties could reach hundreds of billions of dollars. item.title: Iceland votes on whether to resume EU membership negotiations
item.description:
Icelanders will decide tomorrow whether to resume talks on joining the EU in a vote that has taken on deeper significance in the wake of US President Donald Trump’s threats in the Arctic. Polls in the tiny island nation — which does not have armed forces — are almost evenly split. Supporters believe joining the European bloc could give the country greater protection and boost its economy, while critics worry over sovereignty. The Arctic has emerged as a key battleground between global superpowers: Trump has threatened to take over Greenland, an autonomous territory belonging to Denmark. Meanwhile, China is flexing “ its economic muscle in partnership with Russia ” as melting ice caps open up new navigable routes around the Arctic, Bruegel wrote. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh not ruling out interest rate hike amid inflation concerns

Warsh did not indicate where the Fed will take interest rates in the coming months, despite US inflation remaining stubbornly above the central bank’s 2% target amid the war in Iran. But his speech was taken by markets as a signal that rates may rise in the coming months, a move that may put him at odds with Donald Trump , who has aggressively called for rates to be cut. item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln to visit port in Thailand after more than 250 days at sea
item.description:
W hen I was deployed at sea as a junior officer , I used milestones to track the passage of time. Each day counted toward something: a port call, when you get a break on land from the monotony at sea; the “crossing the line ceremony” when a ship crosses the equator (unfortunately, canceled at the last minute for my ship); and, eventually, the date I knew that, no matter what, I would be going home. Even on my worst days, that end point helped me stay focused on the mission and gave me something to be hopeful for. The USS Abraham Lincoln left its home port of San Diego in November and was scheduled to return home in May. That did not happen. In the middle of this month, it surpassed more than 240 consecutive days at sea—one of the longest deployments on record—and had only a brief working port call early last month, where it appears sailors did not disembark, leaving them still at sea…

item.title: Tim Curry, the prolific performer who transformed for the screen – video
item.description:
As a performer, Tim Curry knew how to walk a fine line. Even his most sinister characters had an ironic sort of appeal, because watching Curry have fun is, in itself, fun. The actor, who died yesterday at age 80, acted with palpable glee: He could produce a real-life version of the Grinch’s ever-widening grin and could commit to sheer silliness in a way that freed him to twirl around in a cape while singing a gibberish song about Halloween . Perhaps nowhere was this more evident than in the 1985 film Clue . When the raucous comedy adaptation of the classic whodunit board game debuted in theaters, Paramount Pictures had a unique plan: Instead of one ending, the movie would have three, and audiences never knew which resolution—which killer, in which room, with which weapon—they were going to see. item.title: Lawmakers Want To Stop Kids From Nicknaming Their Pokémon
item.description:
It may sound Farfetch'd , but lawmakers are advancing a bill that would stop minors from nicknaming their Pokémon online—in violation of the First Amendment. Last month, the House of Representatives passed the KIDS Act , a wide-ranging package of youth online safety bills. It includes the Safer GAMING Act , which would require interactive online video games to "limit communication between" players "under the age of 17" and "any other user." That limit must be "enabled by default" and "set to the most restrictive setting," automatically blocking all "verbal, written, or visual messages" to and from minor users. Parents could adjust the safeguard "to a less restrictive setting," but silence is the starting point, in every online game. This sweeping regulation would violate the First Amendment .
